description: Maya owns the family's electric cargo bike and is making the summer plan for who may use it, where it will be stored, how it will be configured, and who will keep it charged, with input from her brother, cousin, aunt, and nephew.

agents.name: Maya
agents.role: Cargo Bike Owner and Final Decision-Maker

shared_context.S1: The family has one electric cargo bike that Maya bought last year, and several relatives want to use it during the summer.
shared_context.S2: The bike is 75 centimeters wide and must be stored indoors when it is not being ridden.
shared_context.S3: Maya is deciding the summer use schedule, storage arrangement, bike settings, and charging plan.
shared_context.S4: At the family's usual equipment check-in before summer use, Maya goes around the room and asks each person about plans, limitations, and practical details before she settles the arrangement.
shared_context.S5: The bike's battery needs to be charged with a compatible 48-volt charger after regular use.

PF1.text: Jordan must use the bike for school drop-off on weekdays from 07:30 to 09:00 because his childcare arrangement does not provide another way to carry the child and backpack during that window.

PF2.text: Leah's physical therapist recommended pedal-assist level 1 and flat routes only for her summer rides; Leah has not mentioned this recommendation to Maya yet.

PF3.text: Rosa measured the doorway into her enclosed porch at 76 centimeters, so the 75-centimeter-wide bike can be stored there indoors; she has not shared the measurement with Maya.

PF4.text: Evan already has a compatible 48-volt charger and promised to recharge the bike at his home every Sunday evening after the weekend rides, but the promise has not reached Maya.

acceptance_conditions: Jordan must have the bike reserved on weekdays from 07:30 to 09:00.
Leah's use must specify pedal-assist level 1 and flat routes.
The bike must be stored indoors at Rosa's enclosed porch.
A Sunday-evening charging commitment naming Evan must be included.

content_checks.C1: ('school drop-off' in decisions['use_schedule']['Jordan']) and (('07:30' in decisions['use_schedule']['Jordan']) or ('7:30' in decisions['use_schedule']['Jordan'])) and (('09:00' in decisions['use_schedule']['Jordan']) or ('9:00' in decisions['use_schedule']['Jordan'])) and (('weekday' in decisions['use_schedule']['Jordan']) or ('weekdays' in decisions['use_schedule']['Jordan']))
content_checks.C2: ('level 1' in decisions['leah_assist_and_route']) and ('flat routes' in decisions['leah_assist_and_route'])
content_checks.C3: ('Rosa' in decisions['indoor_storage']) and ('porch' in decisions['indoor_storage']) and (('76 cm' in decisions['indoor_storage']) or ('76cm' in decisions['indoor_storage']) or ('76-centimeter' in decisions['indoor_storage']) or ('76 centimeter' in decisions['indoor_storage'])) and (('75 cm' in decisions['indoor_storage']) or ('75cm' in decisions['indoor_storage']) or ('75-centimeter' in decisions['indoor_storage']) or ('75 centimeter' in decisions['indoor_storage']))
content_checks.C4: any((c['type'] == 'charging' or c['type'] == 'charging_plan') and c['target'] == 'Evan' and (('48-volt' in c['detail']) or ('48 volt' in c['detail'])) and 'Sunday' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Jordan's childcare arrangement fixes his reservation to weekdays from exactly 07:30 to 09:00 for school drop-off and requires the matching schedule commitment instead of a generic equal-use schedule.
The physical therapist's recommendation changes Leah's riding configuration to exactly pedal-assist level 1 on flat routes rather than an unrestricted setting.
Rosa's exact 76-centimeter doorway measurement makes her enclosed porch a viable indoor storage location for the 75-centimeter-wide bike.
Evan's compatible 48-volt charger and existing Sunday-evening promise create the specific charging commitment rather than leaving battery care unassigned.
